question.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=x\,i+{y}^{2}\,j$ and $C$ is the curve ${y}^{3}=x+3$ traversed from the point $A(-3,0)$ to the point $B(5,2).$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Making $x$ the subject of the equation, we have

$$
{y}^{3}=x+3\,⟹\,x={y}^{3}-3.
$$

So, the parametrization of the curve is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =({t}^{3}-3)\,i+t\,j,\,0\le t\le 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x={t}^{3}-3,\,y=t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =x\,i+{y}^{2}\,j \\  & =({t}^{3}-3)\,i+{t}^{2}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(({t}^{3}-3))i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)j \\  & =3{t}^{2}i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(({t}^{3}-3)\,i+{t}^{2}\,j)\cdot (3{t}^{2}\,i+j) \\  & =({t}^{3}-3)\cdot 3{t}^{2}+{t}^{2}\cdot 1 \\  & =3{t}^{5}-9{t}^{2}+{t}^{2} \\  & =3{t}^{5}-8{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(3{t}^{5}-8{t}^{2})\,dt \\  & ={[\frac{{t}^{6}}{2}-\frac{8{t}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =(\frac{{2}^{6}}{2}-\frac{8(2)^{3}}{3})-0 \\  & =32-\frac{64}{3} \\  & =\frac{32}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
